coverage.assessment: The bluff's logic survives: why he wasn't killed, the password, the goose, the bargain and the date. The 'Dead men tell no tales' line has lost its trigger ('seeing you all face to face'), a cut made in the first draft.

The pronoun in 'The 29th,' he said now attaches to the German. The removed gas-burner line is minor; 018 still says 'towards the gas'. 'The man in the shabby clothes' lacks a 'shabby' antecedent in the 009 revision, which is a neighbour cut and is not charged here.

The Boris exchange cut leaves Tommy's 'And why am I so confident?' unattributed and responding to nothing spoken. 'I like your style' is also unattributed once 'Tommy leaned back wearily' is gone, though context makes the speaker recoverable.
'I have a theory', 'pretty sure of my facts', 'Not in the least' and 'Perhaps' are all preserved. Tommy holds no papers and no location.
The German's curious look, his 'Do you not know that she can tell you nothing?' and the 'factor somewhere' line remain, with no explanation of Jane's memory loss and no hint about the pictures.

The revision cuts the pin-drop pause, the room rising to its feet, and several heartbeat or urbanity markers. This flattens the contrast between Tommy's flippancy and his fear and blunts the build-up to the Lusitania line.
The Mephistopheles-to-Mr. Brown link survives, but the line about the arch-criminal's power growing 'more real' is gone. The living-tomb image is therefore less motivated.
The Faust pictures and the memory-hint dependencies are intact at both ends. The 29th dependency survives verbatim, but its local attribution is compromised by the pronoun.

dependencies.assessment: All four pictures are named neutrally, with no hint of concealment. The partner (026) retains the unhooking of Marguerite with her casket of jewels.

dependencies.assessment: The curious look, 'can tell you nothing' and the 'factor somewhere' line survive unexplained. Partner 019 keeps Tommy's later realisation.

dependencies.assessment: The line survives verbatim and partner 009 has the overheard 'The 29th.' However, with Tommy's action beat cut, 'he said' follows 'said the German', which blurs that the date is Tommy's lever (see F2).

findings.claim: The revision removes Boris's 'Speak!', Tommy's 'Do I look as though…', Boris's 'No… you do not' and the 'mind reader' aside. The next narration still refers to 'his words', and Tommy's next speech answers a question about confidence that no longer exists. It also follows directly on his fear of being seen through, with no speaker tag.
findings.counterevidence: Readers may infer that the speaker is Tommy from 'propose a bargain'.

He looked confidently round, and was glad they could not hear the persistent beating of his heart which gave the lie to his words.

findings.claim: The revision cuts Tommy's reasoning on waking: he was struck while listening, he is known as a spy, nobody knows where he is, and he must rely on his wits. This leaves the 'tight place' generalisation less prepared. The first draft kept most of this reasoning.

strengths: All eight protected verbatim lines are present, including the password hinge, the Tuppence-regret aside and the goose line.
The deliberation interval is kept intact: five minutes of a violent heartbeat alongside flippancy to Conrad, plus the black-cap joke.
The Jane Finn exchange keeps 'To watch her face', the German's uncertainty and the Danvers recovery, all without premature disclosure.
Hunger is retained at the close, supporting the opening of 018. The 'Shall I see him?' / 'Perhaps.' hook is preserved.
summary: The revision keeps the chapter's main plot spine. All eight verbatim lines survive, as do the continuity requirements (Conrad named, Number One absent and unnamed, Boris present, no papers, no memory explanation) and all three dependencies. However, two cuts made in the revision break attribution at key points of the bluff. First, removing the Boris 'Do I look…' exchange leaves 'his words' and 'And why am I so confident?' without an antecedent. Second, removing 'Tommy lay back on the couch' makes 'The 29th,' he said read as the German's line. Smaller losses thin the suspense beats, Tommy's inner fear beneath his flippancy, and the Faust-room mood.
